title: Relative flat-module patching on a space over an infinitesimal scheme pushout
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T_0\hookrightarrow T_1$ be a nilpotent thickening of $S$-schemes, meaning a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $I$ satisfying $I^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$, and let $T_0\to T_2$ be affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $P=T_2\amalg_{T_0}T_1$ be their scheme pushout, which is also their algebraic-space pushout [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout]. Let $h:V\to P$ be any algebraic-space morphism and put $V_i=V\times_PT_i$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Modules are quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]; all pullbacks below are tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For a map $W\to T$ to a scheme, flatness of a module over $T$ means that on etale scheme charts its Zariski stalk at $w$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for the image $t$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Restriction gives an equivalence from the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-modules flat over $P$, with all module homomorphisms, to the category of triples $(M_2,M_1,\alpha)$, where $M_i$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{V_i}$-module flat over $T_i$ for $i=1,2$, and $\alpha:(V_0\to V_2)^*M_2\simeq(V_0\to V_1)^*M_1$; arrows are pairs of module homomorphisms commuting with $\alpha$. The functor sends $M$ to its two restrictions with the canonical pullback-composition comparison. If $h$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], then an object $M$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_V$-module if and only if both restrictions $M_i$ are of finite presentation as $\mathcal O_{V_i}$-modules. Finite presentation of a module means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. No flatness of $h$, properness of a support, separatedness, quasi-compactness, or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Write $j_i:V_i\to V$. Apply [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts] to the identity pair over the scheme pushout $P$ (so its second pushout is again $P$). For every affine open $P_a=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset P$, the three base inverse images are affine, say $T_{2,a}=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T_{1,a}=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $T_{0,a}=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $R=B\times_A A'$. In particular all three $T_i\to P$ are affine, by the defining affine-open test. Their base changes $j_i$ are affine by the same test: over $\operatorname{Spec}D\to P_a$, their inverse images have rings $D\otimes_R B$, $D\otimes_R A'$ and $D\otimes_R A$. The affine-scheme computation is [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and does not identify $D$ with the fibre product of these rings.

source.place: Tag 08KV, affine reduction; More on Morphisms Tag 07RT (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-pushout-along-thickening), compatible affine opens

proof.text: Use affine etale charts $W=\operatorname{Spec}D\to V$ whose maps to $P$ land in some $P_a$. These charts cover $V$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] and [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], a quasi-coherent module on any such chart is its ordinary section module; scheme pullback and etale tensor pullback agree. Apply [lem-pc-affine-pullback-chart-tensor-flat-stalks] with $X=W$, $U=W$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $T=R$ via the identity. The canonical $R\otimes_R L\cong L$ identifies flatness of sections over $R$ with precisely the stalkwise flatness over $P_a$ in the stated definition of relative flatness. Apply the same test with $B,A'$ on the charts of $V_2,V_1$. By [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-point-chart-independence], stalkwise flatness at a point of $V$ over $P$ holds on every etale scheme chart through it as soon as it holds on one; the same applies over $T_2,T_1$ on $V_2,V_1$. Thus all subsequent statements about relative flatness can be checked on these section modules. No flatness of $R\to D$ is used.

source.place: Tag 08KV, affines etale over the source and base; Morphisms of Spaces Tag 05VU (spaces-morphisms.tex, lemma-flat-at-point)

proof.text: Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. On the scheme charts, [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change](1) gives stalkwise flatness over $T_i$ of the pullback of a module flat over $P$ on the charts $W\times_V V_i$, which cover $V_i$; by [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-point-chart-independence] it is then flat over $T_i$ on every etale scheme chart of $V_i$. The comparison on $V_0$ and its compatibility with module maps are the pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. This defines the restriction functor $F$ on all objects and all module homomorphisms, with exactly the comparison specified in the statement.

For a triple $(M_2,M_1,\alpha)$ put $M_0=(V_0\to V_1)^*M_1$ and use $\alpha$ for the map from the other restriction. Form the module sheaf $G(M_2,M_1,\alpha)=j_{2,*}M_2\times_{j_{0,*}M_0}j_{1,*}M_1$, the kernel of the difference of the two restriction maps from the direct sum. These maps are the adjoints of the restriction comparisons. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change], the three direct images are quasi-coherent, and on an etale chart they identify canonically with the direct images from the three base-changed affine schemes. Kernels of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent and are computed on affine charts by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. A compatible pair of module maps induces a map of these kernels, defining $G$ on arrows. This construction is global, so no choice of descent datum is needed.

source.place: Tag 08KV, first displayed formula of the proof

proof.text: On $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ of step 2 put $D_2=D\otimes_R B$, $D_1=D\otimes_R A'$, $D_0=D\otimes_R A$, and let $N,M'$ be the sections of the two given restrictions. The comparison is $D_0$-linear and identifies $N\otimes_B A$ with $M'\otimes_{A'}A=M$. Tensor associativity here is given by $n\otimes(d\otimes a)\mapsto dn\otimes a$, inverse $n\otimes a\mapsto n\otimes(1\otimes a)$; for the quotient use [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring]. Step 4 identifies $G(W)$ with $K=N\times_M M'$. By step 2, $N$ is flat over $B$ and $M'$ over $A'$. Hence [lem-sfb-flat-module-fibre-product-patching] makes $K$ flat over $R$. The isomorphisms [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] give $K\otimes_R B\cong N$ and $K\otimes_R A'\cong M'$; they are $D_2$- and $D_1$-linear since their formulas are $(n,m')\otimes b\mapsto bn$ and $(n,m')\otimes a'\mapsto a'm'$. Thus step 2, with [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-point-chart-independence] for the charts not of this form, proves relative flatness of $G$, and these maps give $FG\cong\mathrm{id}$. Their overlap is the given $\alpha$, by the defining equation of the fibre product.

source.place: Tag 08KV, reduction to Tag 07RW, lemma-relative-flat-module-over-fibre-product; Tag 07RU, canonical recovery maps

proof.text: For a module $L$ flat over $P$, the two adjunction units define $L\to GF(L)$. On the chart of step 2 this is $l\mapsto(l\otimes1,l\otimes1)$, an isomorphism by the flat-module recovery assertion of [lem-sfb-flat-module-fibre-product-patching]. It is $D$-linear since both coordinates are. Its inverse commutes with restriction and module maps because the forward maps do and are invertible; hence the sheaf map is a natural isomorphism. The maps $FG\to\mathrm{id}$ of step 5 are likewise natural by [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change]. In particular a compatible pair of homomorphisms lifts by applying the fibre-product map and the two recovery isomorphisms; a lift is unique because each flat source module is recovered as that fibre product. Consequently $F$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective, with quasi-inverse $G$, including all arrows required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 08KV, quasi-inverse verification, expanding the omitted details

proof.text: Suppose $h$ is locally of finite presentation. At any point of an etale scheme chart of $V$, the chart definition [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] allow affine neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $P_a=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $D$ finitely presented over $R$. They may be chosen anew around each point; no claim that an arbitrary affine restriction is finitely presented is needed. If $M_1,M_2$ are finitely presented, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] makes their section modules $M',N$ finitely presented over $D_1,D_2$. They are flat over $A',B$ by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-fp-module-fp-algebra-pushout] with $E=R$; the identity $R\to R$ is flat directly from $-\otimes_R R\cong\mathrm{id}$. It follows that $G(M_2,M_1,\alpha)(W)=N\times_M M'$ is finitely presented over $D$. The affine-chart criterion then proves finite presentation of $G$ on $V$, hence of its corresponding module by step 6.

source.place: Tag 08KV(b), reduction to Tag 08KP, hypothesis (3) with flat algebra equal to the base

proof.text: Conversely, tensor-pull a local finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^m\to\mathcal O_V^n\to L\to0$ to either $V_i$. Tensor pullback is a left adjoint by [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], so it preserves this cokernel and finite direct sums, and it sends $\mathcal O_V$ to $\mathcal O_{V_i}$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. The pulled-back etale neighbourhoods cover $V_i$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. They therefore give finite presentations of both restrictions. Together with step 7 this proves the asserted if and only if.

lean.statement: theorem restriction_equivalence {S : Scheme.{u}} (D : Diagram S) [IsClosedImmersion D.i.left] [IsAffineHom D.a.left] (hnil : ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ D.i.left.ker ^ n = ⊥) (hpush : IsPushout D.a.left D.i.left D.j₂.left D.j₁.left) : ∃ E : FlatQCoh D.h ≌ FlatTriple D, ∃ (e₂ : E.functor ⋙ leftForget D ≅ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ moduleTensorPullback D.r₂) (e₁ : E.functor ⋙ rightForget D ≅ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ moduleTensorPullback D.r₁), (∀ M : FlatQCoh D.h, (moduleTensorPullback D.a₂).map (e₂.hom.app M) ≫ (restrictionComparison D M.obj).hom = (E.functor.obj M).obj.hom ≫ (moduleTensorPullback D.a₁).map (e₁.hom.app M)) ∧ (MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.h → ∀ M : FlatQCoh D.h, M.obj.IsFinitePresentation ↔ ((moduleTensorPullback D.r₂).obj M.obj).IsFinitePresentation ∧ ((moduleTensorPullback D.r₁).obj M.obj).IsFinitePresentation)
lean.note: The theorem includes the equivalence with natural identifications of both component functors and their overlap compatibility, so its functor is restriction on every object and arrow up to a specified natural isomorphism. Its second conjunct is the finite-presentation iff under local finite presentation of h. Diagram only names arbitrary cartesian inverse images and their uniquely determined overlap maps. Categories and canonical comparisons are explicit helper constructions of this same node; existing relative-flatness, scheme-space and tensor-composition declarations are reused through their landed definition nodes.
